profile.promoter: K K Birla group: the Poddar (Zuari/Adventz), Bhartia (HT Media) and Nopany (SIL) families hold equal-sized blocks; promoters 61.3% (Jun-2026)
profile.hq: New Delhi (registered office Gadepan, Kota, Rajasthan)
profile.plants: Three ammonia-urea plants at one site in Gadepan: G-I (1,767 TPD ammonia, 3,100 TPD urea), G-II (1,710 TPD ammonia, 3,000 TPD urea), G-III (1.27-1.3 mt urea a year, commissioned 2019 under NIP-2012); total 3.4 mt a year; TAN plant (2.4 lakh t TAN, 2.1 lakh t WNA) in commissioning
profile.market: ~10% of India's urea output; largest private-sector urea maker; 14 states (north, central and west), 4,918 dealers and 93,000+ retailers; 'Uttam' brand for non-subsidised products
profile.jv: IMACID (Morocco): 33.33% each with Tata Chemicals and OCP; phosphoric acid 5 lakh t P2O5 a year rising to 7 lakh t (Apr-Jun 2027 per Q1FY27 call); FY26 PAT ₹386 cr (Chambal share ₹128.8 cr)

urea.name: Own manufactured fertilisers (urea)
urea.what: Urea from the three Gadepan plants plus sales of surplus ammonia; revenue is mostly government subsidy (the farm-gate price, MRP, is fixed by the government)
urea.economics: G-I and G-II under NUP-2015 / Modified NPS-III: fixed costs reimbursed, gas cost passed through against energy norms; Chambal runs 4-6% below the G-I/G-II norms and 2-3% below for G-III (Q3FY26 call), so it keeps the energy saving. G-III is priced under NIP-2012 for eight years: a normative price of ~US$285/t at the base gas price plus ~US$20/t for every US$1/mmBtu rise in gas (Q1FY26 call), with a floor and ceiling; the period ends in December 2026 and the follow-on formula was undecided on 30-Sep-2026.

cf.name: Complex fertilisers
cf.what: Imported DAP, TSP, MOP and NPK grades (largely from Russia, some North Africa), plus ammonium sulphate from Q1FY27; NBS subsidy per kg of nutrient
cf.economics: DAP is effectively a fixed-margin product (government compensates about 4% of MRP, ~₹1,026/t per the Q3FY26 call); NPK prices are 'open' but capped by affordability. Profit depends on buying before price rises and on NBS rates.

cpc.name: Crop protection chemicals, speciality nutrients and seeds
cpc.what: Asset-light: products sourced from partners (Nichino, Nutrien; talks with Syngenta, Corteva) and sold under 'Uttam'; biologicals (Uttam Superrhiza, Uttam Pranaam, ~3 million acres treated); seeds since FY25; CFCL-TERI Centre of Excellence for patented biologicals (launches FY29 onwards)
cpc.share: ~3% of CPC & SN market, ~6% of biologicals (Q3FY26 call)

tan.name: Technical ammonium nitrate (Others segment)
tan.what: 2.4 lakh t TAN (HDAN, AN melt) and 2.1 lakh t weak nitric acid at Gadepan; Casale technology; L&T lump-sum turnkey contract; ₹1,645 cr
tan.status: EPC 92% complete at Dec-2025 (₹1,184 cr spent); WNA and AN solution production started in June 2026; HDAN commissioning 'very soon' at 31-Jul; sales capitalised (not in P&L) until the whole project is commissioned; customer tie-ups and warehouses being completed by end-December 2026

nbs.rabi2627: Not announced by 30-Sep-2026 (management on 31-Jul: the government 'might... do something by October'; interim relief sought but not granted). We leave Rabi rates out.

policy.text: MRP fixed by the government; subsidy = cost (gas at pooled price against energy norms + reimbursed fixed costs) less MRP. Production beyond reassessed capacity (RAC) is paid at gas cost plus a fixed component, capped by the import parity price (IPP); IPP was ~US$900/t in May 2026, so above-RAC output was profitable.

Domestic and imported gas for urea is pooled (EPMC); during the West Asia disruption the government prioritised gas to urea plants. Chambal's gas cost: US$14.6/mmBtu (Q3FY26), above US$20 (Mar-2026), US$18-18.5 (May), US$17.25 (Q1FY27 provisional).

Eight-year NIP-2012 period ends December 2026 ('we are to be in this regime from December 1st onwards'). Government 'seized of the matter', file started, data provided; precedent uses net fixed assets and return on net worth, normally over a 15-year depreciation life, but G-III is only eight years old; management will not 'hazard a guess' and says outcome could vary 'both positively and negatively'. It will set the template for Matix and HURL's three plants.

Approved by the CCEA on 15-Jul-2026: 8-9 new gas-based plants (~10 mt), fixed and variable costs separated, ROE band 12-16%, fixed costs converted to INR after four years. Chambal: land, water, railway siding and in-principle gas approval in place, environment clearance in progress, technical bids received, financial bids expected by mid-October 2026; capex ₹9,500-10,000 cr for ~1.3 mt; EBITDA ~₹12,000-13,500/t; commissioning 'within 2030'; returns 'dilutive' vs NIP-2012; subject to Board and DoF approval.
Kharif 2026 rates (+~10% for N, P, S) were set before the post-war spike in ammonia, sulphur and phosphoric acid; industry seeking relief; Rabi 2026-27 rates pending on 30-Sep-2026.
Brought under NBS for Kharif 2026; Chambal launched an AS grade in Q1FY27.

prices.value: US$1,700/t for Jul-Sep 2026 vs US$1,360 in Apr-Jun (Coromandel Q1FY27 call, 31-Jul-2026)

Summer sowing 182.7 lakh ha at 30-Jun-2026 (-23% YoY; oilseeds -53%, cotton -35%); July rains caught up acreage; IMD maintained a normal-monsoon forecast at the 31-Jul call (AR FY26 MD&A had flagged an IMD early forecast of 92% of LPA, El Niño)

WNA and AN solution sales made from June 2026 are credited to the project cost ('decapitalising'), not revenue, until the whole plant is commissioned.
